newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Westinghouse completes Bulgaria reactor test.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse completes Bulgaria reactor test.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp has completed tests of Bulgaria's oldest reactor at Kozloduy after its closure in May amid international concern over safety, an official said on Monday.
Kozloduy nuclear plant spokesman Iordanka Stoyanova said the procedure of taking metal samples from reactor number one had been completed late on Sunday.
"The samples will be transported this week to the (plant's designer) Korchatov's Institute in Russia for analysis," Stoyanova told Reuters by telephone.
The analysis will be carried out under the quality control of Germany's Siemens AG, officials said, adding that Bulgarian experts will also participate in the tests.

Officials had said that Westinghouse had delayed the taking of the samples by a month due to technical difficulties and the delay would prolong the completion of the final results of the metal's tests.
The plant's chairman Kiril Nikolov said the final report would now be expected early next year, while preliminary results could be received by the end of the year.
If the analysis of the samples prove that the metal is in a good condition to continue operating, Bulgaria will restart the reactor, atomic officials said.
Bulgaria switched off its oldest reactor on May 15 under pressure from the European Union, concerned about its safety.

In July Bulgaria signed a financial memorandum with the EU for receiving a grant of 10 million ECUs as compensation for switching off its 440-megawatt Soviet-made reactor and buying alternative energy resources and saving energy.

Bulgaria, poor in energy resources and currently suffering an acute economic crisis, relies for half of its energy on the Kozloduy plant. It has four 440-megawatt reactors and two more modern 1,000 megawatt reactors.
